scope: Python runtime modules under core plus public top-level facades
review_policy: The local quality suite enforces these limits; GitHub CI is disabled. Raising a limit requires an ADR or same-review architecture rationale. Revisit each runtime-line increase after removing comparable code.
runtime_line_budget_rationale: The 283-line increase centralizes descriptor-relative no-follow filesystem helpers, replaces duplicated artifact traversal, applies them to bounded chat file reads, stale-write checked atomic updates, no-overwrite creates, and private long-response artifacts so symlink swaps cannot redirect workspace writes or block reads on named pipes, rejects oversized voice files and stale per-chat transcriptions, redacts known credentials from Telegram network errors and tracebacks before logging, pins task undo deletion and ownership-record reads/updates to one opened root so a root symlink swap cannot redirect removal or metadata writes, and uses dual-clock deadlines so clock corrections cannot extend in-memory approvals and suspend time still expires them. Revisit after removing comparable runtime code. The 39-line increase secures SQLite databases and existing WAL/SHM sidecars with no-follow file descriptors before opening connections, and fails closed on permission or path-race errors. The 7-line increase ensures JobStore closes its SQLite connection when schema initialization fails. The 6-line increase makes bot shutdown attempt every resource close before surfacing the first failure. The 1-line increase resolves the database parent while preserving the final path component so JobStore rejects a pre-existing database symlink without changing its target. The 3-line increase keeps read-only job diagnostics on the requested database path and rejects symlinks before querying them. The 1-line increase applies the same final-component check to the persistent memory database so symlink targets are not chmodded or opened. The 22-line increase runs bounded acceptance commands in isolated POSIX process groups and terminates/reaps the group on timeout so descendants cannot continue changing the workspace. The 42-line increase caps captured acceptance stdout and stderr with the existing bounded stream reader while keeping error output useful and automated commands non-interactive. The 53-line increase propagates multi-agent cancellation through a thread-safe acceptance boundary and kills/reaps the POSIX command group instead of letting checks run until timeout. The 48-line increase registers acceptance process groups in the durable job store so startup recovery can terminate checks orphaned by an application crash. The 19-line increase adds descriptor-anchored os.fwalk deletion on Python 3.10, where shutil.rmtree lacks dir_fd, preserving scoped undo without following symlinks. The 9-line increase serializes previously unlocked MemoryStore reads and scope mutations on its shared SQLite connection, preventing concurrent callers from observing partial scope clears; revisit after equivalent query paths can be simplified. The 55-line increase tracks a delegated run before setup awaits, synchronously cancels active runs on SIGINT, SIGTERM, or SIGABRT before python-telegram-bot drains updates, and awaits process-tree cleanup before closing resources; it also refuses new agent runs during shutdown. Revisit after consolidating lifecycle tracking with the durable job owner. The 11-line increase displays worker expected outputs before approval and includes role, inputs, and outputs in risk detection so a second confirmation covers actions omitted from the top-level goal. The 19-line increase redacts secret-named environment values from every LightClaw log message and exception trace before console and JSONL handlers format records, closing leakage paths from otherwise unfiltered exception handlers. The 15-line increase creates JSONL log files with owner-only permissions, tightens existing files, rejects symlink and non-regular targets, and creates new log directories privately. The 6-line increase makes /clear revoke the current chat's unapproved and time-bounded actions and invalidates in-flight voice transcription so cleared requests cannot be approved later. The 11-line increase centralizes pending-action revocation so /clear scopes it to one chat and confirmed /wipe_memory clears it across chats while active runs remain untouched. The 8-line increase retries Telegram text sends once after a short rate limit and caps the wait at 30 seconds, preventing dropped user-facing results without holding handlers indefinitely. The 2-line increase centralizes one-shot cancellation across Telegram callbacks, signal shutdown, and worker heartbeats, so repeated requests cannot interrupt cleanup. The 1-line increase requires a second confirmation for filesystem move, copy, and replacement commands and correctly matches /etc/ system paths. The 28-line increase applies interaction age retention and the SQLite size ceiling to persisted summaries, discards derived summaries before source interactions under size pressure, and checkpoints after VACUUM to avoid deleting conversation records because of WAL bytes. The 9-line increase binds global memory-wipe confirmations to the initiating Telegram user and the existing dual-clock expiry helper, so shared group state and wall-clock changes cannot satisfy stale destructive confirmations. The 10-line increase keys in-memory summaries, active-summary guards, and invalidation generations by chat, Telegram user, and workspace so shared group chats cannot leak another user’s cached summary or suppress and restore it through concurrent summarization. The 43-line increase adds a byte-bounded, symlink-safe first-text-hunk diff preview in Telegram and trims file lists for phone review while preserving the complete patch attachment. The 19-line increase keeps the no-follow patch descriptor open across Telegram awaits, so replacing the artifact path after summary delivery cannot redirect the attached diff. The 13-line increase bounds the per-user summary cache to 128 least-recently-used entries and retains invalidation generations only while summaries are active, while SQLite remains the durable source. The 18-line increase bounds optional JSONL logging with 5 MiB rotation, three private backups, and 4,096-character free-form field caps, without adding dependencies. The 2-line increase attaches secret redaction to root and JSONL handlers so propagated provider and memory logs cannot bypass the filter. The 50-line increase finalizes abandoned multi-agent runs after orchestration exceptions by stopping workers and heartbeats, failing unfinished lanes, clearing active tracking, and notifying the chat. The 5-line increase rate limits paid voice transcription to six requests per Telegram user per minute before file download. The 3-line increase applies a per-user sliding-window limit to text-triggered model work and rejects excess requests before provider processing. The 9-line increase returns a clear Telegram recovery message when approved multi-agent setup fails before any worker starts; in-flight failures still use durable job finalization. The 58-line increase waits for multi-agent workspace, checkpoint, snapshot, and durable-job filesystem threads to finish across cancellation; a pre-job canceled run removes only its metadata-proven LightClaw workspace, while an existing job or announced workspace is preserved. The 6-line follow-up removes unannounced owned workspaces after ordinary preflight errors as well as cancellation. The 15-line net addition shares cancellation-safe task-workspace creation across single-agent and multi-agent setup, waiting for registration to finish and removing only the newly owned workspace if canceled. The 87-line addition carries the same cancellation guarantees through single-agent checkpoint and durable-job setup, waiting for background operations, canceling persisted lanes before agent launch, clearing active state, and preserving owned workspaces whenever a job record exists; shared workspace helpers keep single and multi setup consistent. The 18-line follow-up cancels durable jobs and clears active run tracking when SQLite or other setup failures occur after job creation but before agent launch. The 30-line follow-up retries one transient SQLite finalization failure and records terminal-state failure in the private receipt when persistence remains unavailable, so completed agent work is not silently lost. The 2-line follow-up logs and retries transient SQLite heartbeat errors so a background task cannot discard a completed run. The 5-line follow-up retries cancellation state writes once and preserves the owned workspace when active-run cancellation encounters a transient SQLite lock. The 3-line follow-up shares transient heartbeat recovery and durable cancellation between single-agent and multi-agent runs. The 7-line net reduction reuses the retrying durable cancellation helper for multi-agent stop handling. The 36-line follow-up shares retrying terminal job writes across single-agent and multi-agent runs and records failed persistence in the multi-agent receipt. The 7-line follow-up waits for the final workspace snapshot and cancels the durable job if the run is interrupted before finalization. The 31-line increase waits for the final snapshot, file-change scan, and patch generation before recording the single-agent terminal state, cancels durable jobs if any of those thread-backed phases is interrupted, marks patch-generation failures as failed jobs, and keeps CLI parsing available to direct execution-mixin consumers while moving that logic beside agent helpers. The 9-line follow-up rejects JSON or Markdown receipts over the existing byte ceiling before either private file is written, keeping writer output readable by the bounded receipt loader. The 11-line increase preserves one-shot task cancellation on Python 3.10, where asyncio.Task.cancelling is absent, while weak task references prevent repeated shutdown and callback cancellation from interrupting cleanup. The 8-line voice-review increase shows captions beside the transcript and rejects requests that cannot fit in one complete Telegram approval message. The 4-line follow-up reports the transcription provider HTTP status without response contents and distinguishes provider failure from a missing API key. The 48-line follow-up tracks active per-session chat requests so /clear can discard queued work and prevent an in-flight reply from restoring cleared history while allowing already-started work to finish. The 13-line follow-up shares the invalidation across `/wipe_memory`, serializes message registration during the global clear, and resumes new requests after the database clear completes. The 2-line follow-up reuses cancellation-safe thread completion for global memory wipes and discards summary caches before releasing chat admission, preventing cancellation from letting new messages race a still-running SQLite clear. The 7-line follow-up keeps cancellation-safe thread waits intact across repeated cancellation requests and reuses that helper during task workspace creation, preventing late filesystem side effects from outliving cleanup. The 3-line net increase shares the cancellation-safe wait between background threads and process cleanup, ensuring repeated cancellation cannot bypass TERM/KILL, stream draining, or process-group unregistration. The 18-line follow-up shields delegated subprocess startup, recovers its process handle after cancellation, and drains both output pipes while terminating before streaming begins; failed registration preserves immediate KILL rather than adding a grace period. The 8-line follow-up binds trusted host-run confirmation to the initiating Telegram user and preserves the pending request when another group member attempts confirmation, keeping sandbox removal under the requester's explicit control. The 4-line follow-up restores terminal slash commands under local stdin authority, preserves their CLI memory scope, accepts keyboard-bearing replies, and decodes escaped HTML for readable terminal reviews. The 63-line follow-up exposes the complete trusted host-run task, binds approval and discard to one random review ID and its requester, rejects incomplete or superseded reviews, and clears failed review delivery without erasing a concurrent replacement; Telegram callbacks reuse the command gate. The 23-line follow-up reuses pending-plan identity for in-flight planning, invalidates an older review when planning starts, and discards superseded, canceled, or memory-cleared planner results across create and edit paths without adding a second state store. The 2-line follow-up applies the existing configured-secret redactor to provider errors before storing fallback planner notes, preserving diagnostics without copying credentials into Telegram reviews. The 25-line follow-up records complete multi-plan review delivery, blocks command, text, and callback approvals or second-confirmation priming until all chunks are sent, and invalidates interrupted delivery only when it still owns the pending request. The 25-line follow-up binds multi-plan command confirmation to its random review ID, binds Telegram yes replies to the final delivered review message, and preserves terminal yes by passing the ID of its fully printed review; missing or stale associations return migration guidance without executing or priming high-risk approval. The 12-line net increase shares memory-clear admission and invalidation between chat requests and heartbeat runs, prevents scheduled results from restoring erased history, skips an unstarted model call after clear, and replaces the removed heartbeat chunker with the existing bounded Telegram HTML chunker. The 11-line follow-up rechecks persisted cron destinations against the current Telegram access policy before sending, pausing revoked private chats and unauthorized groups without deleting their saved jobs. The 4-line follow-up reuses the Telegram HTML chunker for cron listings, keeping complete job IDs and reminder text readable when the list exceeds a single message. The 16-line follow-up validates heartbeat durations with one shared conversion before config acceptance, storage initialization, or schedule replacement, rejecting runtime overflow while preserving an existing schedule. The 5-line follow-up uses the standard-library ExitStack to release each opened database and provider client when bot initialization fails or is interrupted, retaining normal shutdown ownership only after initialization succeeds. The 11-line follow-up makes the Telegram entrypoint own its event loop and retain cleanup ownership until bot shutdown succeeds, draining supervised workers and background tasks before closing resources when startup, polling, or framework teardown fails. The 12-line follow-up reuses registered memory-request tasks and the global wipe lock during shutdown, rejecting new request admission, draining active chat and heartbeat requests, and waiting for a started database wipe before closing storage. The 4-line net reduction replaces the terminal close helper and explicit exit calls with standard-library contextlib.closing, releasing initialized resources after session-binding failures, input errors, and model or command interruptions. The 1-line net increase registers voice requests with the existing shutdown guard and removes their request IDs in identity-checked cleanup, draining Telegram and transcription awaits before resources close without deleting a newer voice request. The 2-line net reduction shares one cancellation snapshot between stop signals and shutdown, canceling registered chat, voice, and heartbeat requests before Telegram drains updates while preserving agent cleanup and excluding the current task. The 5-line increase reuses the existing unsafe-text filter throughout detailed plan reviews, making directional controls, terminal escapes, and invalid Unicode visible before HTML encoding while preserving trusted terminal colors. The 1-line net increase shares the expected-input and expected-output renderer so all worker inputs included in agent instructions and risk detection are visible in the complete human approval review. The 9-line net increase adds an optional byte bound to the existing atomic JSON writer, enforces the same 1 MiB bound for cron reads and writes, and explains a rejected full-store addition without replacing saved reminders with unreadable state. The 8-line net reduction reuses descriptor-based bounded text reads for JSON state, rejecting leaf symlink and FIFO swaps at open time while preserving missing-file defaults and existing parent-directory aliases. The 11-line net reduction replaces handoff resolve-and-check sequences with workspace-rooted JSON reads through existing no-follow directory descriptors, rejecting parent symlink swaps for both worker metadata and explicit handoff checks while retaining unrooted state-file compatibility. The 1-line net reduction reuses nonblocking regular-file reads for personality, heartbeat, and agent authentication text, preserving configured aliases and encodings while rejecting FIFOs and translating Python 3.10 alias-resolution cycles into handled file errors. The 4-line net increase anchors receipt file hashes to the task workspace through existing non-following regular-file descriptors, preventing swapped file or parent symlinks from hashing outside content and rejecting named pipes without waiting. The 15-line net increase shares descriptor-relative metadata checks across required files, globs, reported paths, and deliverable audits, preventing file or parent symlink swaps from falsely satisfying acceptance while preserving internal aliases, directory reports, and metadata-only checks on unreadable files. The 11-line net increase pins acceptance-command working directories through existing non-following directory descriptors and a short isolated Python child that fchdirs, closes the descriptor, and execs the approved command, preventing launch-time symlink redirection without thread-unsafe pre-exec hooks and closing parent descriptors on both launch success and failure. The 7-line net increase shares the existing descriptor-pinned subprocess launcher between acceptance checks and local-agent startup, rejects a swapped workspace before opening, keeps Codex rooted at the opened working directory with -C ., and directs delegated agents to use relative paths rather than a moved workspace label while preserving cancellation cleanup. The 11-line net increase moves the existing directory-pinned command bootstrap into a shared filesystem context manager for asynchronous agent/acceptance launch and synchronous Git artifact operations, preventing workspace swaps from staging, committing, resetting, or inspecting a replacement repository while closing directory descriptors through one shared lifetime. The 1-line net increase keeps PR workspace symlinks visible to the Git launch guard, creates the PR body in a private temporary directory outside the task tree, uses the shared pinned-directory command context for gh creation, and cleans the body on success, failure, or timeout without deleting a file through a replaced workspace path. The 9-line net increase checks provider client closure before every retry and shares a worker-entry closed-state guard across OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini, and direct Anthropic-compatible HTTP calls, so work still queued when shutdown closes the transport cannot start a new SDK or HTTP operation. The 3-line net increase makes the shared token-count converter treat nonfinite numeric telemetry as unavailable rather than discarding valid provider text through NaN conversion or infinity overflow errors, while preserving existing finite token counts and nullable usage. The net-zero provider lifecycle change keeps the request-closed flag set after an SDK cleanup error while tracking successful transport cleanup in the existing adapter owner; the facade forwards repeated closes to that idempotent owner so failed cleanup can be retried without allowing more provider work. The 2-line net increase binds single-agent and multi-agent job claims to the launching run inside the existing SQLite transaction, preserving queue priority while preventing a request from claiming an older run without executing it. The 2-line net increase treats only a missing-process error as proof that a worker PID is absent; denied or failed probes retain the live-writer lock in recovery and diagnostics rather than marking a possibly live run stalled.
